title: Inverse point evaluation preserves K-flat complexes
statement: Let $(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ be a ringed space with exactly one point, and put $A=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$. Let $e:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y)\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(A)$ be an equivalence whose forward functor is naturally isomorphic to global sections [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Assume the inverse functor is additive. If $K$ is an arbitrary unbounded cochain complex of $A$-modules for which tensoring on both sides preserves quasi-isomorphisms, then the termwise image under $e^{-1}$ is K-flat in the acyclic-total-tensor sense [def-pc-kflat-complex] in the category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: One-point sheaves and the empty-open condition; K-flat definition; parent lem-sc-global-tensor-pullback-kflat proof step 1

proof.text: The empty-open section module is zero by the empty-cover sheaf condition (006U). Every open containing the unique point is the whole space. The sectionwise tensor of two module sheaves is therefore again a sheaf: all covering families of a nonempty open contain that open, and the empty sections are zero. Sheafification of this presheaf has its canonical counit isomorphism. Evaluation of the sheaf tensor is consequently naturally isomorphic to the tensor of the evaluated modules.

Termwise evaluation is an exact equivalence because he identifies it with e.functor. It preserves coproducts, and hence the preceding tensor isomorphism identifies total sheaf tensors and total module tensors, including both differentials and their signs. It preserves and reflects acyclicity.

For an acyclic sheaf complex F, evaluate F and use the equivalence counit to identify evaluation of the inverse image of K with K. Tensoring the evaluated F with K is acyclic by the acyclic criterion for ordinary K-flatness (HomotopyCategory.kFlat_iff_preserves_acyclic, a proved declaration). Reflect this acyclicity through evaluation to obtain the sheaf IsKFlat assertion. This applies equally to the zero ring and arbitrary unbounded complexes.

lean.statement:
theorem pointInverseEvaluation_isKFlat
    (Y : RingedSpace.{u}) [Unique Y]
    (e : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y) ≌
      ModuleCat.{u} ((moduleRings Y).obj.obj (op ⊤)))
    (he : Nonempty (e.functor ≅ globalSectionsFunctor Y))
    [e.inverse.Additive]
    (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} ((moduleRings Y).obj.obj (op ⊤))) ℤ)
    (hK : (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso _ (.up ℤ)).kFlat K) :
    CochainComplex.IsAcyclicTensorKFlat (R := Y.sheaf)
      ((e.inverse.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj K)
